concepts.name: Multi-step tool calls and stop conditions

questions.prompt: You're building a command-line chat that prints the answer as it's generated. Which AI SDK function fits, and how do you read its output?

choices.text: `generateText`, then print `text` word by word with a short delay
`streamText`, printing each part as you `for await` over `result.textStream`
`generateText` with `stream: true`, then read `result.textStream`
`streamText`, then print `await result.text` as soon as that promise resolves

questions.explanation: `streamText` starts streaming at once, and `result.textStream` is both a `ReadableStream` and an async iterable of text deltas. `generateText` waits for the full answer, which fits background jobs and agents. `await result.text` also waits for the end, which loses the streaming.

questions.prompt: You wrap `const result = streamText({...})` in `try`/`catch`, but a provider error never reaches your `catch`. Why?

choices.text: `streamText` retries the provider call forever, so it never fails
Errors are thrown only when `maxRetries` is 0; otherwise they're swallowed silently
`streamText` doesn't throw; errors become stream parts, handled with `onError`
Errors are thrown only in server routes, never in a command-line app

questions.explanation: The AI SDK docs warn that `streamText` suppresses errors to keep servers from crashing: errors become part of the stream. Log them with the `onError` callback, or handle `error` parts when you read `result.stream`. `generateText` does throw, so `try`/`catch` works there.

questions.prompt: In AI SDK 6 and later, what is the recommended way to get a Zod-validated object from a model?

choices.text: `generateText` with `output: Output.object({ schema })`; `generateObject` is deprecated
`generateObject({ schema })`, the only AI SDK function that accepts a Zod schema
Ask for JSON in the prompt and run `JSON.parse(result.text)`
Call `generateText`, then run `schema.parse(result)` on the whole returned result object

questions.explanation: The AI SDK 6 migration guide deprecates `generateObject` and `streamObject` in favour of `generateText` and `streamText` with an `output` setting, such as `Output.object`, `Output.array` or `Output.choice`. If the reply can't be parsed or doesn't match the schema, `generateText` rejects with `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`. Prompting for JSON and parsing it yourself skips both the provider's structured-output support and the validation.

questions.prompt: Compare `generateText`, `streamText` and structured output (`output: Output.object(...)`) in the AI SDK. When would you use each?

model_answer.summary: `generateText` returns the finished result, `streamText` streams it as it's generated, and an `output` setting on either one makes the SDK return a schema-validated value instead of free text.
key_points: `generateText` waits for the whole response; good for background jobs, automation and agents that use tools
`streamText` streams as the model generates; good for chat UIs and anything interactive; errors arrive in the stream rather than being thrown
`output: Output.object({ schema })` (AI SDK 6+) validates the reply against a Zod schema and returns it typed
`generateObject`/`streamObject` still appear in older code but are deprecated since AI SDK 6

questions.explanation: The topic list for this Lesson names `generateObject`; in the current AI SDK (7) it is deprecated, so learn the `output` setting and recognise the old name when you meet it.

questions.prompt: In `tool({ description, inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }), execute })`, what does `inputSchema` do?

choices.text: It only types `execute`'s argument at compile time and is never sent to the model at all
It validates the value `execute` returns before it goes back to the model
It gives example inputs that are shown to the user when the tool runs
It tells the model the parameters and validates its tool-call input before `execute`

questions.explanation: The AI SDK docs say the schema is consumed by the LLM and also used to validate its tool calls. `execute` then receives the validated, typed input. `description` helps the model decide when to use the tool. `execute` is optional, for tools whose calls you forward to the client or a queue.

questions.prompt: In a multi-step `generateText` call, your tool's `execute` throws because an API is down. What does the AI SDK do?

choices.text: It adds a `tool-error` part to the step, so the model sees the error next step
It throws `NoSuchToolError` from `generateText` and ends the whole call
It retries `execute` up to `maxRetries` times, then drops the tool call silently
It ends the loop and returns the step's text, ignoring the failed tool

questions.explanation: Errors thrown by `execute` become `tool-error` content parts, which lets the model react in the next step. You can find them in `result.steps`. `NoSuchToolError` means the model called a tool you didn't define, and `maxRetries` retries failed model requests, not tools.

questions.prompt: You call `generateText` with a `weather` tool and no `stopWhen`. The model decides to call `weather`. What do you get back?

choices.text: Two steps: the tool result, then a final answer that uses it
An error, because tools can't be used without setting `stopWhen`
Only the tool call and its result, no answer text: `stopWhen` defaults to `isStepCount(1)`
The model is called repeatedly until it stops calling tools, capped at 20 steps by default

questions.explanation: `generateText` does a single generation by default (`stopWhen` defaults to `isStepCount(1)` in AI SDK 7). A tool call ends that step, so no second call turns the result into an answer. Set `stopWhen: isStepCount(5)`, say, and the SDK sends the tool result back to the model for another step. AI SDK 7 renamed `stepCountIs` to `isStepCount`.

questions.prompt: Why does the AI SDK's `ToolLoopAgent` default to `stopWhen: isStepCount(20)`?

choices.text: 20 is the maximum number of tools one agent may define
A safety limit so a runaway loop can't make endless, costly API calls
Providers reject requests whose history exceeds 20 messages
It sizes the pool of steps that are allowed to run in parallel with each other

questions.explanation: The loop-control docs describe the default of 20 steps as a safety measure against runaway loops and the API calls and cost they bring. Raise it with `isStepCount(50)`, or remove it with `isLoopFinished()` if you have another guard. `WorkflowAgent` has no default limit, so give it one.

questions.prompt: Describe the loop your command-line agent runs when you call `generateText` with tools and `stopWhen: isStepCount(5)`. What happens in each step, and when does it stop?

model_answer.summary: Each step is one model call. When the model calls tools, the SDK validates the input, runs `execute` and sends the results back for another step. It stops when the model answers without calling a tool, or when the stop condition is met.
key_points: The model is called with the messages and the tool definitions
If it returns tool calls, the SDK validates each input against `inputSchema`, runs `execute`, and adds the results to the conversation
Then it calls the model again (a new step) with those results
It stops when the model replies with text and no tool calls, or when `isStepCount(5)` is reached
`result.steps` holds every step's tool calls and results, which you can log

questions.explanation: This is the same loop you wrote by hand in Python, with the SDK doing the bookkeeping. The version matters: AI SDK 7 calls the helper `isStepCount`, and AI SDK 5 and 6 called it `stepCountIs`.

questions.prompt: Your code calls `generateText({ model: openai("<model>"), tools, prompt })` from `@ai-sdk/openai`. What does moving to Anthropic take?

choices.text: Rewriting each tool's schema in Anthropic's `input_schema` JSON format
Converting every message to Anthropic's content-block format yourself before the call
Replacing `generateText` with the Anthropic SDK's `messages.create`
Only installing `@ai-sdk/anthropic` and passing `anthropic("<model>")` as `model`

questions.explanation: Every AI SDK provider implements the same language-model specification, so `generateText`, `streamText`, tools and messages keep the same shape. That is the SDK's main promise: switching providers without rewriting your code. Behaviour still differs between models, so rerun your evals after switching.

questions.prompt: What does a plain string such as `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"` resolve to by default in the AI SDK?

choices.text: The Anthropic provider package, which must be installed
The global provider, which by default is the Vercel AI Gateway
A model registry you must create first with `createProviderRegistry`
An error, because `model` must be a provider object

questions.explanation: A plain model ID string uses the global provider, which defaults to the Vercel AI Gateway and reads the `creator/model-name` format. You can set `globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` to another provider, such as `openai`, at startup.

questions.prompt: How would you set up an AI SDK app so that switching the model behind a feature is a one-line change? What still needs checking after a switch?

model_answer.summary: Refer to models by aliases defined in one place, such as a `customProvider`, and let the SDK's common interface hide the provider differences. Then rerun your evals, because models behave differently.
key_points: All providers implement one language-model interface, so `generateText`, `streamText` and tool calls don't change when the provider does
Define aliases such as `fast` and `smart` in one `customProvider` (or a provider registry), so code names the role, not the model
Provider-specific settings go in `providerOptions`, keeping the rest of the call portable
Rerun your evals after a switch: prompts don't transfer perfectly between models

questions.explanation: The SDK makes the code portable, not the behaviour. The applied-llms authors warn that migrating prompts between models is painful and results can shift noticeably.
